1.title: Hot Soup, Yum!
1.topic: on a cold day Dad makes soup in a big red pot with a yam and ham, and the child blows on the hot cup before sipping (family, food, winter)
sounds: 입을 크게 벌리고 짧게 '아': pot '팟', hot '핫'. '포트', '호트'처럼 '오'로 읽지 않아요.
힘을 빼고 짧게 '이': sip '씹', big '빅'. '시-입'처럼 길게 늘이지 않아요.
x는 'ㅋ+ㅅ' 두 소리를 한 번에: mix '믹스'. 끝의 '스'는 아주 작고 짧게.
1.expression: Say “It is cold.” with a little shiver, read “Mix, mix, mix!” like you are stirring, make “Can I sip it?” go up like a real question, say “Not yet!” like a careful dad, blow softly on “Puff, puff, puff!”, and end with a happy, warm “Hot soup on a cold day!”
practice: Hot soup on a cold day!

2.title: Owen's Hiccups
2.topic: a boy gets hiccups at dinner, his family tries sipping water and holding his breath, and his sister's surprise “Boo!” finally stops them (family, human body, humor)
sounds: t·d 뒤의 -ed는 '이드'를 붙여 한 음절 더: started '스타-티드', counted '카운티드'.
p, f, k 소리 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t: jumped '점프트', laughed '래프트'. '점프드'처럼 '드'를 붙이지 않아요.
sighed의 gh는 소리 없음 '싸이드', laughed의 gh는 f 소리 '래프트'. 같은 gh라도 소리가 달라요!
2.expression: Make every “Hic!” short and bouncy, give Mom a calm voice and Dad a helpful one, count “One, two, three…” slowly and hopefully, sigh on “Will they ever stop?” and let it go up, whisper the tiptoe line, shout “Boo!” loud and sudden, pause on “Everyone waited…”, then cheer “No more hiccups!” and laugh on the last line.
practice: Hold your breath and count to ten.

3.title: How Polar Bears Stay Warm
3.topic: how polar bears survive the Arctic cold: two layers of fur with clear hollow hairs, black skin, a thick layer of blubber, small ears and tail, and wide furry paws with bumps for gripping ice (animals, science, winter)
lines: *Imagine* *living* in a *place* | where *snow* and *ice* *cover* the *ground* | for *most* of the *year*. ↘
*Polar* *bears* *live* in the *Arctic*, | one of the *coldest* *places* on *Earth*. ↘
Its *fur* *looks* *white*, | but *each* *hair* is *really* *clear* and *hollow*, | like a *tiny* *straw*. ↘
Under the *skin* | is a *thick* *layer* of *fat* called *blubber*. | It *keeps* the *heat* *inside*. ↘
A polar bear's *ears* and *tail* are *small*, | so *less* *heat* *escapes*. ↘
Its *big*, *wide* *paws* | have *fur* and *little* *bumps* on the *bottom*. | They *help* the *bear* *walk* on *slippery* *ice* | *without* *falling*. ↘
In *fact*, | polar bears are *so* *good* at *staying* *warm* | that they can get *too* *hot* | when they *run*! ↘
*Next* *time* you *zip* *up* your *coat*, | *think* of the *polar* *bear*. | It *wears* its *coat* *all* *year* *long*! ↘
sounds: AR-ctic, BLUB-ber, SLIP-per-y, HOL-low, es-CAPES, with-OUT
Arctic, blubber, slippery, hollow는 첫 음절에 힘! escapes와 without은 뒤 음절 'CAPES', 'OUT'에 힘을 줘요.
혀를 뒤로 살짝 말고 '어r': fur '퍼r', work '워r크', Earth '어r쓰'. '퍼', '워크'처럼 r을 빼지 않아요.
think, thick, Earth는 혀를 살짝 내밀고 바람만 'θ'. the, their는 같은 자리에서 목을 울리는 'ð'. 'ㅆ'나 'ㄷ'로 바꾸지 않아요.
3.expression: Begin slowly and dreamily on “Imagine…”, read the Arctic line like a nature-show host, ask “How do they stay warm?” clearly and let it fall, count off First / Under the fur / Under the skin like steps in a list, sound amazed on “clear and hollow, like a tiny straw”, add a surprised smile to “they can get too hot when they run!”, and end with a friendly, cozy finish.
practice: one of the coldest places on Earth
a thick layer of fat called blubber
It wears its coat all year long!

4.title: The Accidental Ice Pop
4.topic: the true story of eleven-year-old Frank Epperson, who left a soda drink with a stirring stick outside on a freezing night and invented the frozen pop his children later named the Popsicle (inventions, history, science of freezing)
lines: *More* than a *hundred* *years* *ago*, | on a *chilly* *evening* in *California*, | an *eleven-year-old* *boy* named *Frank* was *mixing* a *drink*. ↘
He *stirred* *flavored* *soda* *powder* | into a *cup* of *water* | with a *wooden* *stick*. ↘
*Then* *something* *distracted* him. | He *ran* *off* to *play*, | *leaving* the *cup* *outside* on the *porch*. ↘
The *next* *morning*, | Frank *found* that his *drink* had *frozen* *solid*, | with the *stick* *standing* *straight* *up* in the *middle*. ↘
He *named* his *invention* the *Epsicle*, | a *mix* of his *last* *name*, *Epperson*, | and the *word* *icicle*. ↘
*Later*, | he *grew* *up* and had *children* of his *own*. | They *called* him *Pop*, | and they *loved* his *treats*. ↘
As a *grown-up*, | Frank *decided* to *share* his *idea* with the *world*, | and the *treat* was *sold* as the *Popsicle*. ↘
sounds: c는 보통 'ㅋ', e·i 앞은 'ㅅ', -cious는 '쉬': delicious '딜리셔스'. accident는 '액시던트'.
4.expression: Start slowly like a storyteller, give “Then something distracted him.” a quick turn, lower your voice on “the story goes”, sound amazed when the stick stands straight up, smile on “It was delicious!”, make “and the name stuck!” a little joke, and end thoughtfully on “a happy accident.”
practice: more than a hundred years ago
